subject: Medieval vault geometry at Wells Cathedral
available_material: Measured plans, orthophotos and downloadable 3D models
app_idea: Lift an arc from the tracing floor and locate the corresponding rib in the vault.
personal_fit_rationale: Lift a mason’s scratched arc into the actual ceiling.

subject: Gem faceting designs
available_material: Printable cutting sheets and 6,948 Gem Cut Studio files. Allowed uses vary by design.
app_idea: Cut a tier of facets and trace a ray through the finished stone.
personal_fit_rationale: Cut a facet, tilt the stone, see where the light goes.

subject: Patterns from surviving garments
available_material: Scaled cutting patterns, object photographs and construction instructions. Coat PDF carries a copyright notice.
app_idea: Match seam edges and watch the back pleat take shape.
personal_fit_rationale: Watch a flat piece become the back of a familiar coat.

subject: Astrolabes
available_material: Instrument photographs and catalog entries searchable by star and town.
app_idea: Find the same star pointer on instruments by different makers.
personal_fit_rationale: Find a star tonight, then find it on engraved brass.

subject: Letterlocking
available_material: Scans, crease patterns and virtual unfolding reconstructions for studied letters.
app_idea: Unfold a packet until the address and the text share one sheet.
personal_fit_rationale: The address stays visible as the letter locks itself.

subject: Manuscript collation
source: Penn Libraries / University of Washington VisColl project
available_material: Models of folded sheets and their positions in manuscript gatherings.
app_idea: Pull out one folded sheet and see which pages come with it.
personal_fit_rationale: Pull one sheet and discover its surprising page partner.

subject: Lighthouse flash characteristics
available_material: Published light characteristics and diagrams of flash patterns.
app_idea: Identify lights on a night horizon from their timing.
personal_fit_rationale: Two lights on a dark horizon make a real position puzzle.

subject: Bach keyboard repertoire
available_material: Public-domain score and recorded performance.
app_idea: Follow a returning fugue subject in score and sound.
personal_fit_rationale: Each returning voice rewards both looking and listening.

subject: Guqin tablature
available_material: Tablature and a modern title-by-title guide.
app_idea: Compare two documented fingerings for the same pitch.
personal_fit_rationale: The fingering is subtle; the sound has to carry it.

subject: Carnatic kṛtis
available_material: Notation and lyrics, including the five-element group.
app_idea: Compare opening phrases across the five temple compositions.
personal_fit_rationale: Following a singer’s slides could beat our piano reading.

subject: Korean time-cell notation
available_material: Woodblock notation with pitch, percussion and words in parallel columns.
app_idea: Follow the melody through a facsimile cell by cell.
personal_fit_rationale: Reading the grid clicks early; the tune must do the rest.

subject: Ottoman and Turkish makam repertoire
available_material: Symbolic scores including TXT and MusicXML. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
app_idea: Trace the refrain through changes of rhythmic cycle.
personal_fit_rationale: A familiar refrain can draw you through unfamiliar music.

subject: Editable classical scores
available_material: LilyPond, engraved scores and MIDI. License varies by edition.
app_idea: Isolate written voices and hear their entrances.
personal_fit_rationale: Enough repertoire to find another exceptional showcase.

subject: Art songs
available_material: CC0 score encodings. Other OpenScore collections include string quartets.
app_idea: Follow the accompaniment under one word of a song.
personal_fit_rationale: Hear the piano change what a sung line seems to mean.

subject: Beethoven string quartets
available_material: Machine-readable harmonic annotations. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
app_idea: Hear a labeled modulation in its musical context.
personal_fit_rationale: Hear a phrase passed around four recognizable players.

subject: Piano performance timing
unit: hours of aligned piano audio and MIDI
available_material: Recorded performances aligned with note timing, velocities and pedals.
app_idea: Compare timing and dynamics across passages.
personal_fit_rationale: Straighten a pianist’s timing, then hear what disappears.

subject: Historical score editions
available_material: Scanned editions and other files with item-specific reuse terms.
app_idea: Compare editions of one passage.
personal_fit_rationale: Rich editions, but page comparison alone has little pull.

subject: Musical source records
available_material: Catalog metadata, some with encoded opening melodies.
app_idea: Trace an opening melody through surviving sources.
personal_fit_rationale: Chasing a tune is fun when the search turns up a surprise.

subject: Church bell ringing
source: Central Council of Church Bell Ringers
available_material: The Central Council maintains a library of named methods. A method specifies how the bells change order from one row to the next.
app_idea: Ring one bell yourself while the others play their parts. Trace where you move in the order.
personal_fit_rationale: Once you grasp the permutation, the payoff mostly repeats.

subject: Reproducing piano rolls
available_material: Stanford distributes raw and expression MIDI and rendered audio derived from rolls.
app_idea: Switch between two renderings of a passage to hear what the expression encoding contributes.
personal_fit_rationale: Watch paper holes become a particular pianist’s timing.

subject: Japanese Go
source: A. E. Brouwer’s game archive at CWI
available_material: Downloadable SGF game records include archives for historical players such as Honinbo Dosaku.
app_idea: Replay a game stone by stone, hide the next move, then reveal what the player chose.
personal_fit_rationale: Guessing the next move is fun if you can read the stakes.

subject: Baseball scorekeeping
available_material: Retrosheet has game-level CSVs going back to 1897, with play-by-play and deduced events where available. Coverage varies by game.
app_idea: Rebuild the field after each recorded play and show which states were deduced.
personal_fit_rationale: One astonishing inning could carry a whole reconstruction.

subject: Court dancing
available_material: Pécour’s printed duets encode paths, steps, and bar lines synchronized with the music. Digitized pages.
app_idea: Scrub a musical bar to see where two dancers cross.
personal_fit_rationale: Two ink paths become two people crossing on one beat.

subject: Broadside ballads
available_material: Single-sheet songs survive with lyrics, tune references or music, and woodcuts. The Bodleian directs readers to its SOLO catalog.
app_idea: Follow one tune or recurring woodcut through sheets telling different stories.
personal_fit_rationale: The hook is hearing one tune tell wildly different stories.

subject: Engineering and architectural surveys
available_material: HABS, HAER, and HALS document more than 40,000 sites and structures across the combined collection, with measured drawings, photographs, and reports. The mix varies by site.
app_idea: Register a section against a photograph, then move the cutting plane through a reconstruction.
personal_fit_rationale: One extraordinary building beats browsing 40,000 plans.

subject: Timber bridges
available_material: The Deer’s Mill covered bridge survey documents a specific Burr arched truss.
app_idea: Peel away the siding and trace one timber from an elevation into the assembled bridge.
personal_fit_rationale: Following a load through the truss gives one solid reveal.

subject: Ship hulls
available_material: The Smithsonian catalogs watercraft plans and sells reproductions of many. Some HAER vessel surveys have digitized body plans, sheer plans, and half-breadths online.
app_idea: Select one station in the side view and watch its cross-section take its place in the hull.
personal_fit_rationale: Watch a few strange curves resolve into a recognizable bow.

subject: Mechanical linkages
available_material: Cornell’s Reuleaux collection includes photographs, dimensions, descriptions, and related models. Its Peaucellier record identifies 39 related straight-line mechanisms.
app_idea: Turn the crank and trace successive joints on different models.
personal_fit_rationale: A rotating crank tracing a perfect straight line is magic.

subject: Steam pumping engines
available_material: The Deer Island engineering report identifies individual cylinders and documents the valve drive, with references to specific photographs.
app_idea: Turn the shaft by hand and watch the corresponding valve lift. Internal dimensions would need separate verification.
personal_fit_rationale: More moving parts could repeat the engine demo’s weakness.

subject: Paper astronomical instruments
available_material: Peter Apian’s sixteenth-century astronomy book contains layered rotating discs used to find planetary positions. The exhibit identifies 21 woodcuts with these devices.
app_idea: Rotate a facsimile disc while keeping the printed scales and cutouts visible.
personal_fit_rationale: Use the rotating paper discs to answer a real sky question.

subject: Mechanical tide prediction
available_material: William Thomson’s 1872 predictor survives with ten adjustable components and pulleys. The museum provides an object record and photographs.
app_idea: Engage one pulley at a time and see how its movement changes the combined curve.
personal_fit_rationale: Turn an 1872 crank and predict high water in a real harbor.

field: Craft, material culture, and everyday life
subject: Andean khipus
available_material: The Open Khipu Repository distributes a SQLite database of recorded cords, knots, colors, and relationships.
app_idea: Reconstruct one recorded object in 3D. Select a cord to see which attributes were observed and where its branches attach. The geometry can be explored even where meaning remains uncertain.
personal_fit_rationale: Follow a branching cord; unknown meanings limit the payoff.

field: Craft, material culture, and everyday life
subject: Weaving
available_material: The Bronsons’ 1817 handbook contains more than thirty numbered drafts with cording and treadling directions. Digitized pages.
app_idea: Step the loom from the draft and trace one diamond in the fabric back to its instructions.
personal_fit_rationale: One treadle change alters every diamond in the finished cloth.

field: Craft, material culture, and everyday life
subject: Dye sample books
available_material: One public-domain trade book has 54 mounted dyed fabric swatches and instructions. Full-size images and a PDF are downloadable.
app_idea: Put the printed recipe beside the actual surviving swatch. Display color can be presented as a reading of the scan.
personal_fit_rationale: Beautiful evidence, but a screen gives little feel for dyeing.

field: Craft, material culture, and everyday life
subject: Early modern recipes
available_material: The Folger pairs digitized recipe manuscripts with volunteer transcriptions and reading copies.
app_idea: Compare the order of operations in several versions of one dish, then open the corresponding handwritten line.
personal_fit_rationale: Cooking one would be more rewarding than comparing texts.

field: Craft, material culture, and everyday life
subject: Restaurant menus
available_material: NYPL documents CSV exports and linked menu, page, item, and dish records, including prices where recorded.
app_idea: Give someone the price of a meal in a particular year and let them order from an actual menu.
personal_fit_rationale: Spend one evening’s wages on dinner in another century.

field: Craft, material culture, and everyday life
subject: Museum objects
available_material: The Met offers a collection CSV and CC0 images for public-domain works under its Open Access initiative.
app_idea: Compare the same kind of tool, vessel, or instrument across makers and centuries.
personal_fit_rationale: A huge collection still needs a particular question.

subject: Ships’ weather logs
available_material: CLIWOC release 2.1 contains digitized observations from ship logbooks, 1750–1854, with a downloadable dataset.
app_idea: Sail one recorded passage day by day and watch the observed wind change along the route.
personal_fit_rationale: Follow one voyage and feel how long contrary winds lasted.

subject: Fire insurance maps
available_material: The Library of Congress indexes Sanborn maps by place and supplies digitized sheets for public-domain editions.
app_idea: Pick one block and compare building footprints and construction symbols across survey years.
personal_fit_rationale: Your own block across a century gives the maps real stakes.

subject: Railways and postal routes
available_material: Historical maps and timetable holdings preserve routes and scheduled stops. Online access varies by title.
app_idea: Ask whether a passenger or letter could make a particular connection using one dated timetable.
personal_fit_rationale: Try to get a letter across a country by Friday in 1890.

subject: Roman coin hoards
source: Coin Hoards of the Roman Empire
available_material: Oxford’s project has a searchable database of hoards and their recorded contents.
app_idea: Open one find and compare the ages and origins of coins buried together.
personal_fit_rationale: One buried purse makes a better mystery than a hoard map.

subject: Local Irish folklore
available_material: The Schools’ Collection gathers accounts written down by schoolchildren in the 1930s, with manuscripts, place information, and transcribed entries.
app_idea: Follow one weather sign, riddle, or place-name story across neighboring schools.
personal_fit_rationale: A familiar place could make two conflicting accounts stick.

subject: Tree rings
available_material: NOAA archives raw ring-width measurements and site chronologies. These are modern measurements of growth reaching back before instruments.
app_idea: Slide two sequences of wide and narrow rings past one another to see how cross-dating works.
personal_fit_rationale: Date an unknown timber by matching its run of bad summers.

subject: Kyoto cherry blossoms
source: Kyoto flowering data and source notes
available_material: Researchers compiled dates of full flowering from historical records extending back to the ninth century. Coverage is intermittent.
app_idea: Open a calendar to the same week across centuries and see which years have a recorded bloom.
personal_fit_rationale: A beautiful long record, probably a short interaction.

subject: Chinese star charts
available_material: The Dunhuang atlas represents more than 1,300 stars on a series of maps. Researchers have studied its projection and identified stars.
app_idea: Unroll the atlas against a modern sky and select a star that can be matched across both.
personal_fit_rationale: Recognize the same sky through someone else’s constellations.

subject: Glass astronomical plates
available_material: Harvard’s plate database can be searched by object or sky position and indicates whether a plate has been scanned.
app_idea: Revisit one patch of sky at successive exposure dates and look for an object whose brightness changes.
personal_fit_rationale: Blink two real exposures and catch a star changing brightness.

field: Images that preserve motion or shape
subject: Multiple-view motion studies
available_material: Muybridge’s plates and catalog document successive exposures, camera angles, and time intervals.
app_idea: Pause a horse mid-stride and switch among the original views.
personal_fit_rationale: Freeze one hoof in midair and switch to the other camera.

field: Images that preserve motion or shape
subject: Early film and recorded sound
available_material: The Library of Congress presents Edison company motion pictures and sound recordings; many films survive through paper prints.
app_idea: Scrub an industrial film frame by frame to see the order of a worker’s movements.
personal_fit_rationale: The right ten seconds of footage matter more than the archive.

field: Images that preserve motion or shape
subject: Fossils and prehistoric artifacts
available_material: Smithsonian Human Origins points to 3D collections for fossils and artifacts. Here the measured surface geometry has already been captured.
app_idea: Rotate two objects into the same orientation and compare a particular ridge, edge, or wear surface.
personal_fit_rationale: Two teeth and a wear question beat a shelf of rotatable skulls.

subject: Bobbin lace prickings and working diagrams
source: University of Arizona Digital Archive of Documents Related to Lace
date_refers_to: Publication of The Art of Bobbin Lace
available_material: Scanned manuals with working instructions, illustrations and finished samples.
app_idea: Cross and twist pairs around pins from a historical pattern, then follow one thread through the finished lace.
personal_fit_rationale: You can read the motion back out of the ornament. A second pattern gives you a reason to try again.

subject: Phonautograms on paper
count_qualifier: Documented across six collections in the 2014 nomination
available_material: Digitized traces and recovered audio for selected recordings, including Au clair de la lune.
app_idea: Scrub the pen line under the 1860 song and adjust the paper speed until the sung phrase sounds plausible. Compare with the researchers’ playback.
personal_fit_rationale: Recognizing a human voice in a line someone drew mechanically in 1860 would carry the whole experience.

subject: Renaissance vocal polyphony
available_material: Downloadable machine-readable vocal scores for multiple composers.
app_idea: Choose a sung phrase and follow it from voice to voice. Mute the leader halfway through and hear which voice carries on.
personal_fit_rationale: The voices give you something beautiful to follow across a whole repertoire. Convincing vocal sound is the hard part.

subject: Chladni plate figures
source: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
available_material: Collection description and images of square and circular brass plates used to demonstrate vibration modes.
app_idea: Bow a virtual plate and change frequency to gather sand along its nodal lines. Compare the simulated shapes with documented figures.
personal_fit_rationale: A note produces a shape you can recognize again by ear.

subject: Apollo 8 Earthrise photography
available_material: Crew photographs, onboard audio and a reconstruction of spacecraft orientation from lunar terrain and timed imagery.
app_idea: Look out a capsule window during the reconstructed roll and try to frame Earthrise. Compare your shot with Anders’s photograph.
personal_fit_rationale: A few seconds of real movement explain why an iconic photograph was possible.

subject: Yucatán forest-floor lidar
available_material: Classified ground points, elevation models and terrain visualizations.
app_idea: Relight one strip of forest floor from several angles and trace low straight ridges that disappear under overhead light.
personal_fit_rationale: Finding geometry for yourself is a strong reveal. Identifying who built a feature needs separate evidence.

subject: Japanese sangaku geometry tablets
available_material: Research feature with historical examples and geometric context. The illustrated problems need manual reconstruction.
app_idea: Rebuild a tablet problem, drag one tangent circle and guess which length ratio survives the motion.
personal_fit_rationale: The inscribed problem sets a goal and the visitor can discover the invariant.

subject: Airfoil section coordinates
source: University of Illinois UIUC Airfoil Coordinates Database
available_material: Downloadable section coordinates and outline plots for individual profiles.
app_idea: Overlay two measured outlines at the same chord, predict which behaves better at low speed and reveal wind-tunnel results for profiles with companion tests.
personal_fit_rationale: Tiny differences in curvature invite comparisons. The measured performance gives the guess a payoff.

subject: Satellite portraits of typhoons
source: National Institute of Informatics Digital Typhoon
available_material: Storm-centered infrared images and associated storm-track data.
app_idea: Synchronize two storms at eye formation and scrub backward to see how differently they organized.
personal_fit_rationale: A storm becomes an individual event you can learn to recognize.

subject: Hand-drawn sunspot observations
available_material: Dated solar disk drawings with sunspot locations and group shapes.
app_idea: Pick a spot on one drawing and find it in subsequent sketches. Use its changing position to estimate the Sun’s rotation.
personal_fit_rationale: You can make a physical measurement from a few sheets of someone’s handwriting.

subject: Louvre aulos reconstruction
available_material: Reconstruction notes, fingering and pitch information, and a performance on a replica.
app_idea: Finger the two reconstructed pipes separately and compare the resulting intervals with a phrase from the replica performance.
personal_fit_rationale: Two melodies under one player’s hands are intriguing. The recorded replica sets a high bar for the interactive sound.

subject: Watermarks in Dutch drawings
available_material: Low-energy X-ray images reveal wire marks and paper structure in collection objects.
app_idea: Overlay two watermarks, align the chain lines and decide whether the sheets could come from the same mould.
personal_fit_rationale: A tiny kink in a wire can turn two anonymous sheets into a detective story.

subject: Inuinnait string figures
available_material: Tutorials demonstrating named figures and the sequence of hand movements.
app_idea: Pause at each transfer, highlight the loop that changes fingers and try it with a length of string.
personal_fit_rationale: The decisive test is whether the figure appears between your own hands.

subject: Japanese manuscript and woodblock maps
count_qualifier: Approximate collection size, including undigitized material
available_material: Historical maps and access to georeferenced examples through Japanese Map Warper.
app_idea: Pin three familiar places on an Edo map and see which streets align when the paper is stretched onto a modern map.
personal_fit_rationale: One recognizable walk could make the map’s priorities immediately legible.

subject: Human motion capture trials
available_material: Skeleton definitions and recorded movement sequences in ASF and AMC files.
app_idea: Hide the object in a pushing trial. Guess what the performer is doing from the feet and shoulders, then reveal the trial description.
personal_fit_rationale: A few moving joints can make you feel the weight of an invisible object.

subject: Vertebrate CT volumes
available_material: Tomographic data and models available through MorphoSource, with access conditions by record.
app_idea: Follow an internal passage through consecutive slices of a turtle skull, then reveal its path in the whole head.
personal_fit_rationale: Following one channel gives the visitor a reason to look inside a skull.

subject: ATP synthase rotor structure
available_material: Deposited cryo-EM structure of bovine ATP synthase in a recorded conformational state.
app_idea: Trace the axle through the molecular structure. Toggle between deposited states to see which parts move together.
personal_fit_rationale: A rotary machine you can recognize at molecular scale. The experimental states supply only snapshots.

subject: Historical photographic lens prescriptions
available_material: Lens section drawings and numerical prescription in the published patent.
app_idea: Trace rays through the patented prescription, remove an element and inspect the change in the off-axis image.
personal_fit_rationale: A small stack of curved glass gets a chance to explain itself through the image it forms.

subject: Pipe organ stoplists
source: Organ Historical Society Pipe Organ Database
available_material: Instrument records, specifications, stoplists and photographs with varying coverage.
app_idea: Hold one key and engage stops from a documented organ to reveal the ranks called for by its specification.
personal_fit_rationale: One key can command a remarkable instrument. Recorded ranks would make the demonstration much more convincing.

subject: Interlocking burr puzzle designs
available_material: Designer’s photographs and descriptions, with piece information for selected puzzles.
app_idea: Reconstruct a documented set of pieces and let the visitor discover the first legal sliding move from the assembled solid.
personal_fit_rationale: The first unexpected movement in a seemingly locked block is its own reward.

subject: Historical paper earthquake records
available_material: Archive guide and historical recording examples. Additional holdings may require a request.
app_idea: Follow the pen on a surviving trace and mark where you first see the shaking emerge above background motion.
personal_fit_rationale: A real pen lends the earthquake immediacy, though a single trace offers limited replay.

subject: Measured Munsell color samples
source: Rochester Institute of Technology Munsell Color Science Laboratory
date_refers_to: Color book and subsequent renotation research
available_material: Downloadable renotation coordinates, including a file for colors represented by physical samples.
app_idea: Build a solid from the measured chips, cut it at one lightness and find which hues extend furthest in chroma. Show approximate screen colors.
personal_fit_rationale: The irregular outline of a measured color system is more surprising than a conventional color wheel.

subject: Kepler stellar light curves
available_material: Time-series photometry and target pixel files.
app_idea: Mark two dips in a star’s brightness and predict when the third will arrive. Reveal the next stretch of telescope data.
personal_fit_rationale: You can find an orbit with your eyes and have a telescope check your prediction.

subject: Mozart piano sonatas
available_material: Annotated scores with phrase, cadence and harmony data.
app_idea: In K. 331, switch between a variation and the corresponding phrase of the theme, then follow the finale, Rondo alla turca.
personal_fit_rationale: A tune you recognize gives you a way into six different variations.

subject: Beethoven piano sonatas
available_material: Annotated piano scores.
app_idea: In the Pathétique slow movement, isolate the melody, pulsing accompaniment and bass, then bring them together.
personal_fit_rationale: The contrast between the singing tune and the pulse should carry on sampled piano.

subject: Schumann Kinderszenen
available_material: Machine-readable scores for the piano cycle.
app_idea: Compare the rocking rhythm of Ritter vom Steckenpferd with the longer phrases of Träumerei.
personal_fit_rationale: A complete book of short pieces whose individual characters are visible and audible.

subject: Corelli trio sonatas
available_material: Encoded scores for two violins and bass across three collections.
app_idea: Track a phrase passing between the violins in Op. 3 while the bass continues underneath.
personal_fit_rationale: Three written lines are easy to follow. Sustained violin playback is the challenge.

subject: Debussy Première Arabesque
available_material: Editable LilyPond score, printable notation and MIDI.
app_idea: Color each hand separately and follow the three-against-two passage until the hands meet on the beat.
personal_fit_rationale: The dots make a rhythm you can hear but might find hard to count immediately legible.

subject: Debussy Suite bergamasque
available_material: Editable scores for Prélude, Menuet, Clair de lune and Passepied.
app_idea: Follow the detached tread in Passepied and listen to how chords decay in the opening of Clair de lune.
personal_fit_rationale: A familiar entry point and four distinct movements. The slow passages depend on convincing resonance.

subject: Grieg Lyric Pieces
available_material: Machine-readable solo piano scores.
app_idea: Explore Op. 12 as a book, starting with Arietta and comparing its melodic motion with Elves’ Dance.
personal_fit_rationale: Contrasting miniatures and a natural book-by-book catalog suit repeat listening.

subject: Chopin mazurkas
available_material: Machine-readable piano scores and annotations.
app_idea: Follow the pulse beneath the melody in the A-minor Mazurka, Op. 17 No. 4.
personal_fit_rationale: One dance form rewards close comparison, though its rhythmic lilt needs expressive playback.

subject: Domenico Scarlatti keyboard sonatas
available_material: Humdrum encodings based on Alessandro Longo’s edition.
app_idea: Find repeated notes and register exchanges, preserving each hand’s color in verified hand-crossing passages.
personal_fit_rationale: Keyboard gestures you can see and hear in a single movement give the catalog a clear focus.

subject: Mussorgsky — Pictures at an Exhibition
available_material: Online score edition. Access and reuse vary by edition and territory.
app_idea: Compare each return of the Promenade with the first walk through the gallery.
personal_fit_rationale: The returning walk ties ten very different pictures together.

subject: Albéniz — Iberia
available_material: Online score edition. Access and reuse vary by edition and territory.
app_idea: Track the dance pulse through one page of Evocación.
personal_fit_rationale: The dance is rewarding to follow once the dense chords are voiced well.

subject: Albéniz — Suite española No.1, Op.47
available_material: Online score edition. Access and reuse vary by edition and territory.
app_idea: Follow the repeated-note pattern in Asturias as the register opens up.
personal_fit_rationale: A guitar-like figure on piano makes Asturias immediately recognizable.

subject: Granados — 12 Danzas españolas
available_material: Online score edition. Access and reuse vary by edition and territory.
app_idea: Set the outer and middle sections of Andaluza side by side.
personal_fit_rationale: Short dances invite comparison of accents across the whole set.

subject: Granados — Goyescas (piano suite)
available_material: Online score edition. Access and reuse vary by edition and territory.
app_idea: Trace the melodic ornaments through the opening of Los requiebros.
personal_fit_rationale: Ornaments can hide the tune unless playback gives it room.

subject: Falla — Fantasía bética
available_material: Online score edition. Access and reuse vary by edition and territory.
app_idea: Separate the melody from the dry repeated attacks beneath it.
personal_fit_rationale: Percussive attacks work well, but repeated chords need careful balance.

subject: Mompou — Impresiones intimas
available_material: Online score edition. Access and reuse vary by edition and territory.
app_idea: Compare the amount of silence around each miniature’s opening phrase.
personal_fit_rationale: Sparse writing makes both the resonance and the silences audible.

subject: Nazareth — Odeon
available_material: Online score edition. Access and reuse vary by edition and territory.
app_idea: Tap the steady beat while watching the tune arrive just before it.
personal_fit_rationale: You can feel the displacement before you can name it.

subject: Nazareth — Brejeiro
available_material: Online score edition. Access and reuse vary by edition and territory.
app_idea: Loop the opening and trade attention between syncopated melody and bass.
personal_fit_rationale: The bass makes the syncopation easy to test by ear.

subject: Gonzaga — Atraente
available_material: Online score edition. Access and reuse vary by edition and territory.
app_idea: Follow a polka phrase through successive returns and isolate the bass on the last pass.
personal_fit_rationale: Two hands are enough to hear a whole dance take shape.

subject: Gonzaga — Gaúcho
available_material: Online score edition. Access and reuse vary by edition and territory.
app_idea: Mark the recurring beat of Corta-jaca and follow accents that slip past it.
personal_fit_rationale: An offbeat accent you can clap makes an immediate way into the score.

subject: Villa-Lobos — A prole do bebê No.1, W140
available_material: Online score edition. Access and reuse vary by edition and territory.
app_idea: Compare the keyboard gestures assigned to each doll.
personal_fit_rationale: Each doll has a keyboard gesture a visitor can come to recognize.

subject: Cervantes — Danzas Cubanas
available_material: Online score edition. Access and reuse vary by edition and territory.
app_idea: Hear two short Cuban dances back to back with the bass patterns highlighted.
personal_fit_rationale: The dances are short enough to compare one rhythmic turn at a time.

subject: Gottschalk — Bamboula, Op.2
available_material: Online score edition. Access and reuse vary by edition and territory.
app_idea: Follow the recurring tune across changes of register and accompaniment.
personal_fit_rationale: A recurrent tune anchors the increasingly showy writing.

subject: Gottschalk — Le banjo, Op.15
available_material: Online score edition. Access and reuse vary by edition and territory.
app_idea: Identify the attacks that let a piano imitate a plucked string.
personal_fit_rationale: Plucked-string imitation gives the visitor a specific sound to listen for.

subject: Dett — In the Bottoms
available_material: Online score edition. Access and reuse vary by edition and territory.
app_idea: Follow the separate attack patterns of the hands in Juba, the finale.
personal_fit_rationale: Juba makes independent rhythms into a game you can tap along with.

subject: Price — At the Cotton Gin
available_material: Online score edition. Access and reuse vary by edition and territory.
app_idea: Loop the opening figure and hear what continues underneath the tune.
personal_fit_rationale: The repeated motion gives a short piece a clear visual identity.

subject: Coleridge-Taylor — 24 Negro Melodies, Op.59
available_material: Online score edition. Access and reuse vary by edition and territory.
app_idea: Follow one spiritual melody as the surrounding piano harmony changes.
personal_fit_rationale: A known melody stays traceable inside a much richer setting.
